Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Mark (Crescent CTO), Lena (Crescent Head of Data), Ravi (Crescent SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick cost economics talk, focused on batching/caching, reserved capacity, pilot pricing. Action items at end.

Topics: pricing per token, batching and cache levers, Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, SLA and security, pilot next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros real fast. I'm Evan on the account team, Priya and Jonah are our SEs.
[00:12] Mark: Hey yep Mark here, lena and ravi with me. thanks.
[00:16] Evan: Awesome. Today we wanted to focus on cost per unit, how you might control spend with batching/caching, and what tradeoffs you get between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. sound right?
[00:28] Lena: Yeah that's right. Our main ask - we have an internal budget of about $30k/month for NLP features and we need to understand the per-token economics so we can size a pilot.
[00:39] Priya: Great. quick baseline: for Redwood Hosted, our published per-token rates vary by model and throughput. as a ballpark for the models you're looking at, you should expect something in the range of $0.0006 to $0.0015 per token for generation-heavy workloads - again depends on model size and whether streaming or prompt+response.
[00:58] Mark: okay can you break that down a bit? like where does that number come from, and how would batching move it?
[01:08] Priya: Sure. so two components - compute cost per token and overheads (network, orchestration, margin). compute is largely GPU time per token; if you can increase batch size and amortize kernel launches, effective compute per token drops. with continuous batching the runtime can group requests in micro-batches; for many workloads we've seen 20-30% reduction in unit cost at moderate batching for seq lengths ~512. prefix / KV caching also helps a lot when you have repeated prompts or long context reuse - that eliminates re-computation on the repeated prefix and can drive costs down further.
[01:44] Jonah: to add, caching is particularly impactful for chat-style flows where the conversation history is reused. we have both prefix caching and KV cache optimizations; e.g., if 40% of tokens are repeated prefixes we can cut the token compute by ~40% for that portion.
[01:58] Lena: hmm our use case is customer support summarization - typical prompt 200 tokens, returned summary 120 tokens, but many prompts share a standard preamble. so sounds promising.
[02:08] Mark: what's the tradeoff for latency? we can't tolerate >300ms tail latency on small requests. if batching increases latency are we out of luck?
[02:18] Priya: good question. batching is workload-aware; you can set latency SLOs and the router will favor latency vs cost. we support per-route latency targets - for sub-300ms you can run at minimal batching (slightly higher unit cost) or run Dedicated to get better predictable tails. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, so you don't wait on noisy neighbor or routing variance.
[02:39] Ravi: on Dedicated pricing, how granular are commits and what is the uplift vs Hosted?
[02:44] Evan: Dedicated is typically contracted as reserved GPU capacity - monthly or annual. we give committed throughput guarantees. rough rule of thumb is Dedicated will lower unit cost by 25-40% compared to equivalent Hosted pricing if you fully utilize the reserved capacity; exact depends on utilization and model family. we can run committed capacity sized to your QPS profile.
[03:05] Mark: ok so with our 30k/mo budget - rough math - can you run a sample TCO? we estimate 100k gen tokens/day currently.
[03:15] Priya: sure quick calc: 100k tokens/day ~ 3M tokens/month. at $0.0009/token (midpoint hosted) that's about $2.7k/mo compute - that seems low so maybe I misunderstood your token accounting?
[03:28] Lena: oh right my bad - we meant 100k requests/day at average 300 output tokens each, so ~30M tokens/day. yikes.
[03:38] Priya: ah ok that changes it: 30M tokens/day -> ~900M tokens/mo. at $0.0009/token that's $810k/mo hosted. so obviously huge.
[03:50] Mark: yeah that's why we're talking - we don't want to pay that. are there levers to bring it into our 30k/mo ballpark?
[03:58] Priya: so you have a few axes: reduce token count (shorter prompts, more efficient prompts), caching (avoid re-sending repeated prefixes), batching (amortize overheads), quantized model variants, and workload routing (use smaller model for low-criticality queries). sometimes hybrid works: host sensitive requests on Private/Dedicated and low-critical on cheaper open models.
[04:18] Jonah: also consider rate-limiting and gating at app layer - sample only 10% of requests for full generation and use a cheaper classifier for the rest.
[04:25] Ravi: caching sounds good, but how often do you see real savings - like can caching realistically cut 90%?
[04:32] Priya: 90% is rare; typical wins depend on how much of the token stream is repeated. with heavy reuse (templates, system prompts) you can see 40-60% token compute reduction on that traffic. combined with model distillation/quantization and routing, total TCO sometimes drops 70% vs naive hosted.
[04:51] Mark: what's quantization impact?
[04:54] Priya: 8-bit or 4-bit quant can reduce GPU memory and speed up inference; on some models it reduces cost per token by 20-50% depending on kernel availability. note quality tradeoffs: we recommend evaluating on your eval set. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[05:12] Lena: ok that helps. what about Private (VPC/on-prem)? our compliance team may require it and they assume on-prem is cheaper long-term.
[05:22] Evan: Private adds infra and ops overhead; on-prem has capital and ops cost. for steady-state, very high throughput, on-prem can be cheaper, but remember you need to include SRE costs, hardware refresh, and slower time-to-model-updates. VPC Private (cloud-hosted but in your VPC) is a middle ground - you get control and some isolation without full ops.
[05:45] Mark: and encryption/KMS? our legal needs KMS+HSM and audit logs.
[05:50] Evan: yes we support KMS integrations, audit logs, SOC2 reports. we'll share the security pack.
[05:56] Priya: to make this concrete let's propose a pilot: 3-month reserved Dedicated for a specific model family, include a caching config and an initial TCO sheet. we'll run a bench with your prompt set to give per-token effective cost under realistic batching and cache scenarios.
[06:10] Mark: sounds good. what's pilot pricing?
[06:13] Evan: pilot pricing is flexible - we can do a subsidized pilot or discounted reserved capacity. i'll put options in the TCO spreadsheet.
[06:20] Ravi: also need to confirm latency under 300ms for the short flows. can you guarantee?
[06:25] Priya: Dedicated plus low-latency scheduling typically meets that; we'll include p95 and p99 numbers from similar customers and run the bench to validate.
[06:33] Lena: for bench, we'll provide 5 sample flows, QPS pattern, and expected concurrency.
[06:38] Jonah: perfect. we'll also instrument token-level cost breakdown and show where savings come from (caching hit rates, batching gains, model size decisions).
[06:47] Evan: ok wrapping up - recap of next steps: Evan send TCO and pilot pricing, Priya & Jonah prepare bench plan, Lena send prompt set by Fri. schedule bench for week of Mar 9.
[06:58] Mark: yep that works. thanks.
[07:01] Evan: thanks all.
